title: On hypocrisy (Jer 9:8): peace on the lips, enmity in the heart
english: [[He speaks peaceably to his neighbor, but in himself he holds enmity >> Bible:Jeremiah 9:8]]. The scribes and Pharisees would not have inherited so many [[woes >> Bible:Matthew 23:13]] from the Savior except for hypocrisy: he kept naming them whitewashed tombs, fair outside and full of dead bones within. If we do good to the neighbor through unfeigned love, we hear, [[as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me >> Bible:Matthew 25:40]]; and if through deceitful hypocrisy we show evil to a brother, we sin against God as well. Hypocrisy is a dread enemy, brothers — hidden deceit in the heart set to trap the simple.

title: Uncircumcised in heart among those with the law
english: Does the word mean that the sons of Israel seem to have the law of circumcision yet differ nothing from the uncircumcised nations — themselves uncircumcised in heart, not cut off from their vices? So Gregory presses Jeremiah’s charge: outward cutting is empty when the heart stays Moab’s.

title: Circumcision in Egypt and in the wilderness
english: Why recount all this? He seeks those circumcised in Egypt and those in the wilderness whom the word records. They seem of Ishmael’s line, who dwelt in the desert and took an Egyptian wife — so the catalogue of “circumcised” peoples is not a blank myth but a map of who cuts the flesh without the heart.

title: Edom, Ammon, and Moab in the circumcision list
english: Abraham handed circumcision to his sons and somehow circumcised Edom as well — so the list is no longer obscure. And the sons of Ammon and Moab? Careful readers know them as Lot’s sons, Abraham’s nephew; each was born of Lot’s daughters. The fragment closes by tying Jeremiah’s roll of nations to that kinship map.
